lines.text: Am I confident I actually understand the problem? Sometimes I think the problem is this, it's that. There's a thing in biblical counseling called the presenting problem.

Does this problem really need to be solved right away? Because a lot of times the thing that's called for is just carefully monitoring the situation, but don't touch it.
Am I approaching this problem as a child of God who has been adopted in Christ? Like, am I approaching this problem as if the creator of the universe has bent over backwards to make me his son?

lines.text: From verse 49, Jesus is saying to us this morning that we as Christians never have to be powerless.
He wants to get our attention and make us aware of our need, our daily need for divine power.
Jesus is not reluctant to fill us with his Spirit and to give us power if we will only ask, because it's a promise he has given us.

In our weakest moments, when we are most tired, when we don't want to serve, those are the times when we can be most effective in ministry and to serve others if we will only ask for the Spirit's presence and for the Spirit's power.

lines.text: The pattern is simply this: the gospel transforms lives and it stirs up persecution. The gospel brings redemption and it brings opposition. The gospel saves and the gospel divides.
The Spirit preserved it for us so that we would learn from what we read and not be surprised when people we care about, people we love, reject the gospel and even become hostile towards us.
The gospel is a call to abandon all allegiance to self and sin and the enticements of this world for an allegiance to something much better, which is Christ himself.
It is pathetic, and it is pitiable, because it's not cool. It's compromise.
We have to keep being amazed by what Jesus has done for us and to us. That might be the most important sentence in my manuscript. We have to keep being amazed by Jesus.
When God saves you, He doesn't give you just part of Jesus. He doesn't forgive half of your sins and then leave you to see how you do with the rest.
We possess Christ completely. You, as a Christian, you have Christ completely. And yet, you're not yet a complete Christian.
The truth that Christ is enough That you have all of Christ does not mean you have nowhere left to grow, that you can stop growing, or that there is not growth still in front of you.
Paul, he wants the truth of God's word, the truth of God's revealed will in our heads because he wants obedience in our hands and in our hearts.
That's why when we say Christ is enough, which is what Colossians is all about, Christ is enough, that should never produce lazy, stagnant Christians.
That's why the Gospel isn't just a message that we believe once so that we can be forgiven and converted to Christianity. No, the gospel, it keeps working.
You haven't outgrown the gospel. You never will. And you have a lifetime ahead of you of walking in what God has already given you in Christ.

lines.text: Paul, very familiar with the Jewish mind and heart, walks into their very normal lives, and knowing exactly where to look, he reveals what is ultimately going wrong.

God's true people are not marked by race. They're not marked by family tradition or ceremony. They are marked by something that none of them can do themselves. They are marked by the divine work on the hearts.

He wants us all to understand that no matter what we do, Covenant people or not, Jewish or Gentile, God is never, ever at fault, and our sins are judged rightly by him without any culpability on his part.
God has proven Himself to be beyond faithful to the people, even when they constantly remained unfaithful.
God is always just. Always. He is simply just and righteous. Thus, Paul is able to turn the debate on its head and state with all purity that God is just and his being just will not change.
He is tearing down our hiding places so that the only place left to run is grace.
Far more than the news of God's judgment, this is the story of how we can stop fighting, stop pretending there's nothing wrong, stop pretending it's not our fault, and rest.
The real question was what was it resting on? And that is a picture of the 2 ways to live.
Ultimately, this trust in man, this trust in the world is fundamentally just a trust in self.
Even that goodness which keeps them from seeing their need for salvation is a form of being cursed.
There is a significantly infinite difference between God and man. Why would you choose one over the other?
Even if this should happen, my God's got me. Even if this should happen, my God is good.
